LOGIC STATEMENTS & CONNECTIVES

Logic operates on the basic rule that something cannot be both true and false at the same time. This means that each logic statement results in only one of the two possibilities, either the statement is true or the statement is false. Two other symbols used to join logic statements result in conditional and biconditional statements. Conditioned Connectors Conditioned: If...,then... Biconditional: if and only if

Let's learn more about the "If..., then...'' conditional. conditional: if and only if

A conditional statement means that one condition implies another. We must remember that each individual logic statement, like P, may be either true or false. P : You finished this objective. Q : You will pass the final quiz. PQ: If you finished this objective, then you will pass the final quiz.

COMPOUND STATEMENTS & ARGUMENTS

Once you understand the basic principles of logic statements and connectives you can further manipulate these statements. P: Today is Saturday. Q: Today is Sunday. R: The time is after 4:00 pm. (PVQ) R: Today is Saturday or Sunday and the time is after 4:00 pm PVQ Today is Saturday or today is Sunday. P Today is not Saturday. Q Therefore, today is Sunday.
(PVQ) A R: Today is Saturday or Sunday and the time is after 4:00 pm
PVQ Today is Saturday or today is Sunday.
